L42: 
L43: * * *
L44: 
L45: Update on April 22, 2026: ChatGPT for Google Sheets is now available in beta. We've also added support for app integrations and skills for both ChatGPT for Excel and ChatGPT for Google Sheets.
L46: 
L47: * * *
L48: Today, we’re introducing cite5†ChatGPT for Excel⁠(opens in a new window)†chatgpt.com in beta, an Excel add-in that brings ChatGPT directly into workbooks to help build and update models, run scenarios, and generate outputs based on cells and formulas. Powered by GPT‑5.4, it helps users do more in Excel, supports power users in moving faster, and can improve consistency across teams.
L49: We’re also adding financial data integrations directly in ChatGPT for FactSet, Dow Jones Factiva, LSEG, Daloopa, S&P Global, and more, making it easier to work with trusted financial data inside ChatGPT. Together, these capabilities help teams spend less time on manual work and more time on analysis, decisions, and execution.
L50: ## An AI model optimized for finance workflows
L51: GPT‑5.4 (as GPT‑5.4 Thinking) is available today in ChatGPT, Codex, and the API. It’s our most advanced model, ideal for financial reasoning and Excel-based modeling. We’ve worked closely with industry practitioners to improve GPT‑5.4 on real-world finance workflows that often take analysts hours or days to complete, including financial modeling, scenario analysis, data extraction, and long-form research. The result is stronger performance on the tasks finance professionals rely on every day.
L52: On OpenAI’s internal investment banking benchmark, which evaluates real-world workflows such as building a three-statement model with proper formatting and citations, performance improved from 43.7% with GPT‑5 to 87.3% with GPT‑5.4 Thinking.
L53: ## ChatGPT for Excel in beta: build, update, and analyze spreadsheet models directly in your workbook
L54: 
L55: We’re introducing ChatGPT for Excel in beta—a version of ChatGPT embedded directly in spreadsheets that can build, analyze, and update models using the same formulas and structures teams already rely on. Analysts, strategists, researchers, and accountants can move faster, reduce manual work, and focus on judgment and decision-making instead of writing formulas, tracing links, and fixing models.
L56: #### How it works
L57: 
L58:   * Build and update spreadsheet models faster. Instead of building spreadsheet models or running scenario analysis manually, teams can describe what they need in plain language, and ChatGPT will create or update live Excel models directly in the workbook. Teams can run data analysis, reporting, inventory management, budgeting—all while preserving structure, formulas, and assumptions in a formatted, Excel-native workbook.
L59:   * Get insights from large spreadsheets without manual reconciliation. ChatGPT can reason across workbooks, understand how sheets and formulas connect across the model, explain why outputs changed, trace and fix errors, and show how assumptions flow through a model. This is especially useful when users inherit existing templates, need to get up to speed quickly, or want to understand and test a workbook before making decisions.
L60:   * Follow the logic and trust the outputs. ChatGPT explains what it’s doing as it works and links answers to the exact cells it references and updates. Because calculations run directly in Excel, teams can trace assumptions, audit formulas, and verify how results were produced. Before making changes to a workbook, ChatGPT asks for permission, so users can review each step and undo edits if needed.
L61: #### Known limitations in beta
L62: 
L63: We are improving ChatGPT for Excel quickly based on user feedback. Some responses may take longer as we optimize performance, and generated outputs may occasionally require cleanup or adjustment to match preferred spreadsheet formatting or layout conventions. ChatGPT can generate and explain formulas, but complex formulas or edge cases may still require manual refinement.
L64: #### Getting started
L65: 
L66: cite5†ChatGPT for Excel ⁠(opens in a new window)†chatgpt.com in beta is available globally to ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Edu, Teachers, and K-12 users, and to ChatGPT Pro and Plus users outside the EU. ChatGPT for Google Sheets is coming soon.
L67: 
L68: In Enterprise, Edu, and Teacher workspaces, access is off by default. Admins can enable it for specific users with custom roles and group permissions.
L69: ## Financial data integrations in ChatGPT
L70: For teams working in financial workflows, new data integrations and support for proprietary data through building your own apps using cite15†Model Context Protocol (MCP)⁠(opens in a new window)†help.openai.com , make it easier to bring market, company, and internal data into a single workflow in ChatGPT.
L71: With GPT‑5.4, ChatGPT can handle longer context and more complex tasks, helping teams move faster on company research, model refreshes, and cited outputs for valuation, diligence, underwriting, and related work.
L72: Simplify research and analysis
L73: 
L74: Integrations released today—including Moody’s, Dow Jones Factiva, MSCI, Third Bridge, and MT Newswires, with FactSet coming soon—bring market, company, and internal data into a single workflow in ChatGPT, as part of a growing ecosystem of apps. This helps users spend less time gathering inputs to produce cited outputs such as earnings summaries, valuation snapshots, and credit memos faster. cite16†Explore apps⁠(opens in a new window)†chatgpt.com today.
L75: Quickly conduct due diligence
L76: 
L77: Teams can also use apps with research in ChatGPT to pull from filings, transcripts, decks, and spreadsheets to produce structured, cited outputs that export to PDF or Microsoft Word. Recent updates give users more control over the research process, including the ability to focus on specific websites and data sources, shape the research plan before and during a run, and review sources and citations in a redesigned workspace.
L78: ## Security, governance, and control
L79: 
L80: For organizations adopting ChatGPT at work, ChatGPT Enterprise includes the security, governance, and access controls needed to use ChatGPT confidently, especially in regulated or data-sensitive environments:
L81: 
L82:   * Manage and monitor access with RBAC, SAML SSO, SCIM, and audit logs, with support for common DLP and SIEM tools.
L83: 
L84:   * Protect firm data with encryption in transit with TLS 1.2+ and at rest with AES-256, plus enterprise key management support.
L85:   * Meet regional data requirements with data residency and regional processing controls.
L86: 
L87:   * By default, data shared with ChatGPT Enterprise is not used to train or improve our models.
L88: 
L89: cite17†Read more⁠⁠ about our enterprise-grade security, privacy, and compliance programs. cite4†Contact our team⁠⁠ to learn more.
L90: ## Customer impact
L91: 
L92: We’re working closely with financial institutions as they apply ChatGPT across research, underwriting, auditing, client engagement, code modernization, and operations. Across banks, asset managers, and insurance, we’re seeing impact in workflows like due diligence, client experience, and investment research—and we’ll keep learning alongside customers as they scale their AI deployments.
L93: Hg BBVA Walleye Capital Balyasny Asset Management (BAM)Fidelity International MUFG CommBank Datasite

L96: ## Looking ahead
L97: 
L98: This launch builds on OpenAI’s ongoing work with analysts, strategists, researchers, and accountants. We’re learning from real-world deployments to improve our products and models and help institutions move faster while operating responsibly in regulated environments.
L99: To learn more, cite4†contact our team⁠ . Enterprise customers can build directly with OpenAI or work alongside experienced partners such as Accenture, Bain, Boston Consulting Group (BCG), McKinsey & Company, and PwC to integrate AI into existing data, applications, and operating models.

L26:   * cite4†What you’ll find here L27:   * cite5†How we’ll support you going forward L28: 
L29: A new phase of enterprise AI is underway.
L30: For the past two years, the story was largely about the pace of the technology: new models, new capabilities, new breakthroughs and demonstrations of what AI could do. That phase mattered. But it also created an information environment dominated by technical updates, product news, and benchmark performances which are not the bottleneck to adoption and value anymore.
L31: The defining question for leaders is no longer what AI can do but how to turn that capability into concrete operational change: better decisions, faster workflows, stronger execution, new forms of leverage, and ultimately new business models.
L32: 
L33: That shift calls for a different kind of channel.
L34: That is why we are launching the Adoption channel, a new OpenAI business blog focused on the practical realities of AI at work: how successful organizations scale adoption, build trust with their users, redesign work, and create a durable advantage.
L35: 
L36: This channel is for leaders navigating that transition: C Level executives, heads of AI, transformation and adoption leaders, and the operators and advisors helping enterprises adapt to an AI-native world.
L37: ### What you’ll find here
L38: 
L39:   1. Where AI creates value and what "good" looks like: Clear thinking on where AI drives meaningful business value, how leaders should evaluate opportunity, and what strong execution looks like in practice.
L40: 
L41:   2. How organizations successfully scale AI: Practical insight into what helps adoption spread, what causes it to stall, and how leading organizations move from experimentation to real operating change.
L42:   3. How AI reshapes operating models and roles: What changes when AI becomes part of daily work: how responsibilities shift, how leaders govern differently, and how organizations design for trust, control, and performance.
L43: 
L44:   4. What’s durable versus hype in the AI market: A grounded view of what matters, what is noise, and which developments are likely to shape enterprise decisions in lasting ways.
L45:   5. Vertical perspectives anchored in enterprise realities: How these questions play out differently across industries, with attention to real constraints, systems, workflows, and regulatory environments.
L46: For this, we will explore and share frameworks, decision lenses, operating patterns, and examples from the field. More than anything else, we’ll share concrete explanations of what leading organizations are doing differently. Our goal is not just to describe where AI is going, but to help leaders decide what to do next.
L47: ### How we’ll support you going forward
L48: 
L49: We’ll keep the writing direct, rigorous, and useful: short enough for executives to read, substantive enough to help you decide, and grounded in implementation realities.
L50: 
L51: If you are building in this space, shaping operating models, or guiding adoption, we designed this resource for you. AI is changing work quickly and our goal is to help leaders drive that change with clarity and confidence.
L52: 
L53: Welcome to Adoption news. Follow us to start building your advantage.

L14: # VfL Wolfsburg turns ChatGPT into a club-wide capability
L15: 
L16: By focusing on people, not pilots, the Bundesliga club is scaling efficiency, creativity, and knowledge—without losing its football identity.

L55: At VfL Wolfsburg, football is built on discipline, continuity, and trust. For nearly three decades, the club has been a constant presence in the Bundesliga—backed by strong men’s and women’s teams, a future-oriented academy, and a fast-evolving digital and commercial ecosystem.
L56: But modern football is no longer defined by performance on the pitch alone. Expectations from fans, partners, and internal stakeholders continue to rise—while budgets and headcount cannot scale indefinitely.
L57: 
L58: This tension between growing expectations and limited scalability created a clear need for new ways of working. The question was how to apply it in a way that felt credible in one of the world’s most heritage-driven sectors.
L59: > “In football, tradition is an important value. Change isn’t always easy. But innovation is part of our DNA—and we couldn’t just keep adding people while the workload kept growing.”
L60: 
L61: Linus Lebugle, Head of Business Development
L62: 
L63: Across the club, the same challenges kept appearing:
L64: 
L65:   * Repetitive drafting, translation, reporting, and documentation slowed teams down
L66: 
L67:   * Critical knowledge sat with a few specialists, creating bottlenecks
L68:   * External agencies handled routine work, but at high cost and without building internal capability
L69: 
L70: These challenges highlighted a core tension: the club needed to increase impact and consistency—without increasing headcount.
L71: ## Why ChatGPT Enterprise
L72: 
L73: After evaluating multiple tools and approaches, VfL Wolfsburg chose ChatGPT Enterprise for a combination of reasons.
L74: 
L75: Over the previous year, the club had already built meaningful experience with Generative AI, working with ChatGPT Team and Business licenses. Trained teams, established use cases, and visible day-to-day impact demonstrated clear value, but scaling was limited by access and governance.
L76: “Once we saw trained teams, real use cases, and measurable impact, the question wasn’t whether AI works,” says Lebugle. “The question was how to scale it properly and responsibly across the entire organization.”
L77: 
L78:   * Strong output quality for day-to-day knowledge work
L79: 
L80:   * Enterprise-grade security and governance, including EU server options; OpenAI does not use customer data to train models
L81: 
L82:   * Fast time-to-value without heavy IT build-out
L83: 
L84:   * Intuitive usability that works across non-technical roles

L94: ## Leadership lessons
L95: 
L96: VfL Wolfsburg began focusing on Generative AI in 2023 with a clear mindset: this would not be a niche innovation project or a future experiment. It would be a capability built across the club, with people at the center.
L97: 
L98: Adoption accelerated when Wolfsburg stopped talking about abstract AI tools and started building custom GPTs around real workflows.
L99: 
L100: A few standout examples include Turf Disease GPT, Football School Invoicing GPT, Hannah (HR GPT Builder), and ESG Check GPT.
L101: ## What’s next
L102: 
L103: With proven use cases, trained teams, and growing internal momentum, VfL Wolfsburg is now moving from targeted adoption to organization-wide capability.
L104: 
L105: Beyond internal productivity, VfL Wolfsburg also sees long-term potential in selected fan- and partner-facing experiences—such as personalization, internationalization, and interactive content formats—once governance, operating models, and accountability structures are fully mature.
L106: “AI is not a future topic in football anymore—it’s something leaders need to take seriously today,” adds Meeske.
